member.name: T:System.Windows.FiletypeAssociation.SetFiletypeAssociation
member.summary: Registers a file type for the current user by writing the classic association keys under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes. This sets the *fallback* handler: it works when the user has not yet chosen a default, but will NOT override a default the user already picked. To force the effective default, use SetFiletypeAssociationProtected instead. Runs while Execute is true - connect a bang.

member.name: T:System.Windows.FiletypeAssociation.SetFiletypeAssociationProtected
member.summary:
Sets the *effective* default handler for a file extension on Windows 10/11 by writing a valid, hash-protected UserChoice key for the current user (the reverse-engineered SetUserFTA algorithm). Unlike SetFileAssociations, this overrides an existing UserChoice. Runs while Execute is true.
Note: this relies on undocumented Windows internals. It works for normal extensions but not for types guarded by the UserChoice Protection Driver (UCPD.sys), e.g. browsers and .pdf. Must run as the interactive user.

member.summary: Forces the *effective* default app for a file extension on Windows 10/11 by writing the hash-protected UserChoice key for the current user. Unlike SetFiletypeAssociation, this overrides an existing default that the user already picked. Works for normal extensions (e.g. .vl), but NOT for types Windows guards specially such as browsers and .pdf. Runs while Execute is true - connect a bang.
member.param: True if the new default was written and Windows accepted it.
The Base64 UserChoice hash that was written (diagnostics only).
Message of the last error, or empty if the last apply succeeded.
Path to the program that should open the file, e.g. the vvvv.exe.
File extension to associate, with the leading dot, e.g. '.vl'.
Internal identifier registered for this file type, e.g. 'vvvv'. Any unique name; reuse the same one to update an existing association.
Friendly name shown for the file type in Explorer, e.g. 'vvvv gamma document'.
What is passed to the program after the .exe path. Use %1 as the placeholder for the double-clicked file. Default "%1" just opens the file; e.g. '-o "%1"' adds a flag in front.
While true, (re)applies the association every frame. Connect a bang to do it once.
